parsed.explanation: No traveller-facing restriction is documented: no entry/document rules, facility bans, or custody rules aimed at trans visitors. Criminalisation was repealed decades ago; the constitution (2019) names gender identity, and state institutions run a trans-rights programme with police and courts. The worst documented features are dated police campaigns against gender presentation (2001, 2004) — no post-2004 enforcement is recorded — plus an authoritarian context: LGBTI activists monitored, asylum-seekers prosecuted as traitors (a citizens-only exposure), and Family Code rights 'contested rather than uniformly enforced'. Current police posture is unknown; thin-data extrapolation runs both ways — an episodic enforcement history and state monitoring pull down, while sustained official acceptance programming and an annual pride march pull up. No trans-violence data exists (undocumented, not assessed). This sits as reduced risk with real uncertainty and an unconsolidated settlement, above dead-letter-statute profiles like Valess but below the verified-protection 0.75 tier: 0.68.
